chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Sa'd ibn Tareef, from Al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever follows a funeral, Allah will write for him four Qirats: one Qirat for following it, one Qirat for the prayer over it, one Qirat for waiting until the burial is completed, and one Qirat for the consolation.'
ai.seo_question: What are the four spiritual rewards for following a funeral procession in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the comprehensive spiritual value of funeral etiquette in Shia tradition, attributing four distinct Qirats of reward to the specific acts of following the coffin, offering the funeral prayer, waiting for burial, and providing consolation. The inclusion of 'waiting until burial' underscores the importance of sustained presence and support, while 'consolation' (Taziyah) emphasizes the social and emotional duties of the community. This framework transforms funeral attendance from a passive obligation into a multi-layered act of worship with tangible spiritual dividends.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Husay Bin Ulwan, from Sa’ad Bin Tareyf, from Al Asbagh Bin Nubata who said,

‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘The one who follows a coffin, Allahazwj would Write four Carats for him – a Carat for following it, and a Carat for the praying of Salaat over him, and a Carat for the waiting until they are free from his burial, and a Carat for the consolation’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Husayn ibn ‘Ulwan from Sa‘d ibn Tarif from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah who has said the following: “’

Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If one escorts the body of a deceased, his reward is four qirat, one for escorting, one for Salah (prayer) for a deceased, one for waiting until burial is complete and one for offering condolences.’”
